purpose: Read book presence and a lamp together, then connect the four joint masses to row and column marginals.
meaning: A joint distribution assigns probabilities to pairs of random-variable values. Summing out one variable gives a marginal distribution; dividing a positive-probability slice gives a conditional distribution.

definition.setting: An assumed binary library return-tray model: X records book presence and Y records the sensor lamp.
definition.formal_latex: p_{00}=(1-q)(1-e),\quad p_{01}=(1-q)e,\quad p_{10}=qe,\quad p_{11}=q(1-e),\quad \sum_{x,y}p_{xy}=1.\quad p_X(x)=\sum_y p_{xy},\quad p_Y(y)=\sum_x p_{xy},\quad P(X=x\mid Y=y)=p_{xy}/p_Y(y)\ (p_Y(y)>0).

signature.Y: Binary sensor-lamp random variable: 0 off, 1 on.

signature.e: Symmetric channel flip probability, the same for each input state.
signature.yₛ: Selected observed lamp value, either 0 or 1.
signature.p₀₀: Joint probability of an empty tray and lamp off.
signature.p₀₁: Joint probability of an empty tray and lamp on.
signature.p₁₀: Joint probability of a book and lamp off.

signature.p_X(x): Marginal probability P(X=x), after summing over Y.
signature.p_Y(y): Marginal probability P(Y=y), after summing over X.
signature.P(X=x|Y=y): Conditional probability in a positive-probability lamp column.
signature.pᵢⱼ: Joint probability P(X=i,Y=j), with book index first and lamp index second.
signature.H(X,Y): Entropy of the complete pair of random variables, measured in bits.

conditions: X records presence in one library return tray: 0 means empty and 1 means a book. Y records its sensor lamp: 0 means off and 1 means on. This binary presence model differs from the preceding lesson’s three possible book counts. The channel probabilities are assumed for teaching, not fitted sensor measurements.

The prior book probability q=P(X=1) and symmetric flip probability e lie in [0,1]. The same channel rule gives P(Y≠X|X=x)=e for each possible input value x; a row with zero prior mass still has a specified channel rule.
The joint masses are p₀₀=(1−q)(1−e), p₀₁=(1−q)e, p₁₀=qe and p₁₁=q(1−e). The first index belongs to X and the second to Y. All four masses are nonnegative and add to one.
Marginal distributions come from summing rows or columns. A conditional distribution given Y=y is formed only when P(Y=y)>0; then divide the selected column by its total.
The selected lamp value yₛ is a view selection. Changing it does not alter the joint distribution or any averaged entropy or mutual information.
definition.domain_notes: This finite family is a binary symmetric channel, not an arbitrary joint-table editor. The primary result is the book/on joint mass p₁₁. A selected impossible lamp state has no conditional distribution.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level sources and original finite calculations; independent review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: p_{00}=(1-q)(1-e),\quad p_{01}=(1-q)e,\quad p_{10}=qe,\quad p_{11}=q(1-e),\quad \sum_{x,y}p_{xy}=1.\quad p_X(x)=\sum_y p_{xy},\quad p_Y(y)=\sum_x p_{xy},\quad P(X=x\mid Y=y)=p_{xy}/p_Y(y)\ (p_Y(y)>0).
grammar.formation_rule: First use q and 1−q for the book-presence probabilities. Split each row with channel probabilities 1−e and e, keeping the X index first and Y index second. Sum the joint masses across the other variable to get a marginal distribution. Divide a selected lamp column by its positive marginal total to obtain the conditional distribution.
grammar.precedence: Multiply the prior by a channel probability to form a joint cell. Add cells to form marginals. Normalize only positive-probability conditioning columns, then apply base-two entropy formulas.

prompts.prompt: Is lamp on the same event as book and lamp on?
prompts.answer: No. The lamp marginal adds both book states in that column; the joint event selects one cell.

prompts.prompt: Can a valid joint distribution contain an impossible observation?
prompts.answer: Yes. Its zero column remains valid joint data but cannot be normalized into a conditional distribution.
